slides.title: Posters overnight
slides.text: Posters appear all over Netville overnight, promising free game gems to everyone. Pim tilts her head. Free gems for the whole town sounds too good.
slides.alt: A trick card from the Game Shop, a sender nobody knows: free coins today only, tap the button to claim them.

focus.cue: Free coins today only: a poster in letter form
Too good to be true has cues: free, hurry, tap now

slides.title: The crown jewels
slides.text: Real shops sell their best gems to stay open, so they do not give away the crown jewels. Too-good posters share clues: a miracle prize, a famous singer's face, or you are the millionth visitor.
slides.alt: Spot the Trick opens its first message card: friendly words on the surface, and clues hiding in the text.

focus.cue: You won a tablet: a prize for a contest you never entered
Hurry, asks for your key, says congratulations

slides.title: Check the facts
slides.text: Adverts are allowed to exaggerate to sound exciting. A fact is different: facts need a second source you can trust before you believe them.
slides.alt: Checking the message: the first clue is marked, and the card still has more of its tricks to find.

focus.cue: One cue found: hurry, only ten minutes
Read the letter itself before you believe a word

slides.title: The Defender pause
slides.text: An amazing claim is a signal to pause, not to share. Slow down and check it like a Cyber Defender.
steps: Believe it only if it checks out
slides.alt: Spot the Trick opens its first message card: friendly words on the surface, and clues hiding in the text.

focus.cue: Tap every cue that smells like a trick, then decide
The pause ends in a calm choice, never a fast tap

slides.title: Gems of gravel
slides.text: Then Pim finds gravel scattered behind the posters, and one cheeky feather. The posters were the Magpie's work, and the gems were only gravel.
slides.alt: A trick card from the Game Shop, a sender nobody knows: free coins today only, tap the button to claim them.

focus.cue: From the Game Shop: an unknown sender
The shiny promise, word for word

words.means: a poster or message that tries to sell or promote something
something said as if it were true
where a fact or story comes from

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Play Would You Rather first: choose the Online topic and play Online: share or keep. Then open Packet Post at Spot the Trick and check the prize cards.
slides.alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.

focus.cue: Start with Online: share or keep
